title: Carlsen Returns, Divya Deshmukh Debuts: The Global Chess League Draft Arrives in Mumbai Tomorrow
excerpt: The Season 4 player draft features 36 Grandmasters — including five-time world champion Viswanathan Anand — as six franchises build squads for Bengaluru in September.
body:
The Global Chess League is about to begin its most anticipated season yet, and the opening act takes place not on the board but around a table in Mumbai.

On Sunday, June 29, the six GCL franchises will gather for the Season 4 Player Draft, picking from a pool of 36 Grandmasters to assemble their six-player squads ahead of the league's fourth edition in Bengaluru from September 3 to 13.

The headline names alone tell you how seriously the chess world is taking this. Magnus Carlsen, the world No. 1 who skipped Season 3, is back. Divya Deshmukh, the reigning FIDE Women's World Cup champion, will make her GCL debut. And Viswanathan Anand — the man who made chess a household name in India — is available once more.

## How the Draft Works

Each team must build a balanced six-player squad across four categories: one Icon, two Superstar Men, two Superstar Women, and one Prodigy. The format is six-board rapid chess, where every board carries equal weight. That design forces franchises to think beyond star power — team composition matters as much as individual brilliance.

The full player pool reads like a who's who of modern chess. Alongside Carlsen, Anand, and Deshmukh, franchises can bid for 2025 FIDE World Cup winner Javokhir Sindarov, Women's World Rapid Champion Koneru Humpy, World Championship challenger Ian Nepomniachtchi, former World Cup champion Levon Aronian, reigning World Rapid Champion Volodar Murzin, and Indian Grandmaster Leon Luke Mendonca. Former Women's World Champion Alexandra Kosteniuk rounds out a marquee list that blends proven champions with emerging talent.

## Six Franchises, One Title to Defend

The defending champions, Alpine SG Pipers, return after a dominant Season 3 campaign. They'll face familiar rivals in the upGrad Mumba Masters, Fyers American Gambits, Ganges Grandmasters, Triveni Continental Kings, and PBG Alaskan Knights — all of whom will be looking to unseat them.

Season 3, hosted in India for the first time, set new benchmarks for the league with packed arenas, AI-powered in-arena innovations, and expanded broadcast reach. The move to Bengaluru — a city with deep chess culture and a thriving tech ecosystem — signals the league's continued commitment to building its Indian base.

## India's Chess Moment

The timing could not be better for Indian chess. D Gukesh holds the classical world championship title. Arjun Erigaisi just won the Bullet Chess Championship. Praggnanandhaa, Nihal Sarin, and Vaishali Rameshbabu have all competed in previous GCL seasons. Now Divya Deshmukh, still only 19, adds another Indian name to the franchise circuit after her Women's World Cup triumph.

For NRIs watching from abroad, the GCL represents something broader: an Indian-backed league (Tech Mahindra is co-founder alongside FIDE) that is reshaping how elite chess is consumed worldwide. The franchise-based, mixed-team format is designed for broadcast, with rapid-fire matches and narrative arcs that franchise sport demands.

"The Global Chess League has played a pivotal role in transforming chess into a more dynamic and spectator-friendly sport," said Gourav Rakshit, the league's commissioner. "India's passion for the game and its rapidly growing chess ecosystem make it a natural destination for the league."

## What to Watch For

The draft itself will reveal the strategic hand each franchise wants to play. Will a team build around Carlsen as their Icon and gamble on a lesser-known Prodigy? Will the Ganges Grandmasters try to retain Anand, their iconic Board 1 from Season 1? Can anyone pry Humpy and Deshmukh onto the same roster for an Indian women's powerhouse?

Those questions get answered tomorrow in Mumbai. The chess begins in Bengaluru three months later. For Indian fans — and the diaspora watching this sport transform before their eyes — the wait is almost over.

*The Global Chess League Season 4 will be held in Bengaluru from September 3 to 13, 2026. The player draft takes place in Mumbai on June 29.*
